content:
If you have been a heavy user of the Apple Watch beta this summer, you may have noticed that some existing apps fail to launch on watchOS 27. Apple has identified the issue and is automatically updating apps on behalf of developers to ensure compatibility.

This update is delivered via the App Store, and the "What's New" section reads: "This app has been updated by Apple to prepare it for compatibility with watchOS 27. No new features have been added."

Apple notified developers this week that the process will be completed by August 31.

watchOS 27 (along with iOS 27 and other new operating systems) is expected to be released to the public around mid-September, so the necessary updates are being rolled out with plenty of time to spare.

Apple said this measure was necessary due to an issue with the arm64 sections of some watchOS apps. It appears they are automatically reprocessing and repackaging the affected apps to fix binary compatibility issues, allowing existing apps to continue working normally without any action required from developers.
